subject: Climate & Environment
title: Cities Leading the Way
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cities Leading the Way.

hook.text: While nations debate, cities act. Over 11,000 cities have made climate commitments.

buildup.text: Copenhagen aims for carbon neutrality by 2025. Stockholm is already close. Freiburg runs on solar.

discovery.text: C40 is a network of 100 major cities committed to halving emissions by 2030.

twist.text: Cities control land use, transport, and buildings — the levers that matter most for emissions.

climax.text: When one city proves something works, others copy it. Urban innovation spreads fast.

punchline.text: Nations talk about the future. Cities are building it.

quiz.question: What is C40?
options: A network of 100 major cities committed to climate action

details.summary: Cities like Copenhagen, Singapore, Medellin, and Freiburg are global leaders in sustainable urbanism. Copenhagen aims to be carbon neutral by 2025 through cycling infrastructure and wind power. Medellin transformed slums with cable cars and green corridors. Each city proves innovation is possible.
details.whyItMatters: Pioneering cities demonstrate that ambitious sustainability goals are achievable. Their models inspire and inform thousands of other cities facing similar challenges.
takeaways: Medellin used transit and greening to transform informal areas
Singapore maximizes density with extensive green infrastructure

faq.question: How did Medellin transform its most underserved neighborhoods?
faq.answer: Medellin built cable cars connecting hilltop slums to the metro, added escalators on steep slopes, created libraries and parks in neglected areas, and invested in green corridors. These projects dramatically improved mobility, safety, and quality of life.

faq.question: What makes Singapore a model for sustainable density?
faq.answer: Singapore houses 5.5 million people on 730 square kilometers with extensive public transit, mandatory green building standards, rooftop gardens, vertical greenery, integrated water management, and world-class waste-to-energy facilities.
